newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korea to buy soymeal, tapioca.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korea to buy soymeal, tapioca.

text.p: South Korean feed milling firms and Japanese vegetable oil makers are seen buying soymeal for June delivery, but other East Asian buyers are seen sitting back due to volatile Chicago futures prices, traders said on Monday.
The Korea Feed Association is expected to seek 50,000 tonnes of soymeal while Big Feed Mills is likely to pick up 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of tapioca for June shipment this week, a local trader said.

South Korean traders said they anticipate further falls in soybean prices in Chicago on market talk that the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will not reduce its soybean ending stocks in this week's report.

The May contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed on Friday 30 U.S. cents down at US$8.41 a bushel on news Brazilian soybean exports are headed for the U.S. and on heavy commodity fund selling, U.S. traders said.
"Market sentiment has changed this week to bearish from previously bullish," the South Korean trader said.
In Japan, vegetable oil makers who have already covered U.S. soybeans for May shipment, are likely continue to buy for June deliveries this week, traders said.
"Local buyers are a bit sidelined because of recent volatility in the soybean market. But some will continue to buy this week," one Japanese trader said.
In Taiwan, the pork industry crisis which has hit corn imports is also continuing to pinch soybean imports.
"Corn and soybean inventories are still too high," Taiwan Formosa Oilseed manager Steven Kuo told Reuters.

Taiwan's soybean imports are seen falling about 10 percent this year as demand for soymeal is reduced by weak demand from feedmillers due to the ban on pork imports by Taiwan's major markets in Japan and South Korea.
Traders said many Taiwan soybean processors have already reduced or temporarily halted their crushing operations.
Aside from some spot buying by Japan and South Korea, the only recently concluded deal was the purchase by a Philippine company of 15,000 tonnes of soybeans last week.
There was no price available for the soybeans, although U.S. beans coming into Southeast Asia fetched a quote on Thursday of $355-$360 a tonne C&F for May/June delivery on a Panamax.
